reason: The passage (Exodus 15, the Song of Moses) explicitly demonstrates Yahweh's care for the Israelites through multiple expressions: (1) The explicit invocation of Yahweh's salvation—'עָזִּי וְזִמְרָת יָהּ וַיְהִי־ לִי לִישׁוּעָה' ('My strength and song is Yah, and he has become my salvation'); (2) The critical verse 15:13, which uses the word חַסְדְּךָ (hesed—covenant love/mercy): 'You have led in Your mercy the people you have redeemed; you have guided them in Your strength'; (3) The protective care demonstrated by defeating Pharaoh's pursuing army; (4) The promissory care shown in 'You will bring them and plant them in the mountain of Your inheritance...the place You have made for Your dwelling, O Lord'—indicating Yahweh's intention to establish them in blessing and security. The entire narrative arc moves from deliverance (protective care) through guidance (relational care) to settlement in a promised place (providential care).
